summary: This document deprecates the BGP Entropy Label Capability attribute defined in RFC 6790. That RFC required routers that cannot process Entropy Labels to remove the attribute, but this cannot be guaranteed in practice, so the attribute is unreliable.

eli5.summary: A rule said some routers must erase a note, but they often did not, so the note could mislead. This document says to stop using that note.

questions: why was the bgp elca deprecated
what is the entropy label capability attribute
subtitle: Retires the BGP Entropy Label Capability attribute, which could not work as an optional transitive attribute.

tldr.problem: The Entropy Label Capability attribute (ELCA) must be removed by nodes that cannot process entropy labels, but as an optional, transitive attribute it is propagated by exactly those nodes.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC deprecates ELCA: implementations MUST NOT generate it, and a received one is treated as any unrecognized optional, transitive attribute.
tldr.outcome: IANA marked attribute 28 as deprecated, and a forthcoming document was expected to propose a replacement.

today: RFC 7447 is a Proposed Standard from February 2015 that updates RFC 6790 by deprecating its ELCA attribute. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 6790 defines the Entropy Label Capability attribute (ELCA), an optional, transitive BGP path attribute. A node that changes the next hop of a route must remove the ELCA unless it can process entropy labels.

That requirement cannot be met. By definition a node that does not support an optional, transitive attribute propagates it (RFC 4271), and such a node is likely unable to process entropy labels, which makes it exactly the node that should remove it.
sections.eli5: The rule asked the very routers that do not understand the note to be the ones to throw it away. They never could.

sections.title: Deprecation of ELCA
sections.content:
Implementations MUST NOT generate the attribute. If it is received, it MUST be treated like any other unrecognized optional, transitive attribute, until and unless the code point is reused by a new specification. To the authors' best knowledge there were no implementations of ELCA at the time of writing.

Only the version defined in Section 5.2 of RFC 6790 is deprecated; all other sections are unchanged, and a forthcoming document was to propose a replacement.
sections.eli5: Stop writing the note. If you see one, just pass it along like any other mystery note.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA marked attribute 28, "BGP Entropy Label Capability Attribute", in the "BGP Path Attributes" registry as deprecated and added a reference to this RFC.
sections.eli5: The official list now says this item is retired.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Like other optional, transitive attributes, ELCA is tunneled through routers that do not implement it. Implementations that receive such an attribute could improperly rely on it, which could cause a black hole in the forwarding path. Whether this is a new security issue is debatable, since an attacker would need to be on the control-plane path. Deprecating ELCA makes the issue moot.
sections.eli5: A misleading note could send traffic nowhere. Retiring the note removes the problem.

references.text: Kompella, K., et al., "The Use of Entropy Labels in MPLS Forwarding", RFC 6790, November 2012.
